task.title: Release lines by major or minor version
task.shortdesc: Each release line has one live release. Lines group releases by major version, or by minor version for products whose customers are each on a specific 0.x minor.

context.p: A reader is served the live release of their own line, worked out from the version they are served: their organization's version, or the one the version picker gives them. By default a line is a major version: 2.1 and 2.4 readers both read line 2, whose live release is the newest 2.x build. A product released as 0.21, 0.22 and 0.23 needs a line per minor version instead, or every 0.x reader gets the newest 0.x docs.

strow.stentry: The live 0.22 build, or "No documentation has been published for release 0.22.x yet"

step.cmd: Choose lines by minor version for the repository: in the admin console, on the Site & access page under Release lines, select By minor version and Save release lines; or through the admin API.

stepxmp.p: Or give releaseLines when registering the repository with POST /admin/api/repos, or in a seed file next to the repository: releaseLines: minor. Or let the repository say so, in the site block of its opend.config.yaml: site: { releaseLines: minor }. The first build that goes live switches the lines, and the console then shows the setting read-only ().

info.p: The change applies at once, in one transaction, to what is already live: each live release moves to the line its release belongs to. Nothing that is not live comes back by itself: after switching from major to minor, line 0 becomes the line of its live release (say 0.23), and older minors go live again with their next build (request one with POST /admin/api/repos/:id/builds). Switching back merges lines, keeping the newest build of each. A build that finishes during the switch publishes to a line of the new setting. The change is audited as repo.release-lines, and every replica drops its caches. The console's form does the same, audited under the staff reader's name; saving the grouping already in place changes nothing. See .

step.cmd: Publish each minor from its own branch, for example docs/0.23 with releaseRefs ["docs/*"], and release: "0.23.0" in that branch's opend.config.yaml.

info.p: See . GET /admin/api/repos/1/releases lists the live line of each.

section.title: With the version picker
section.p: A version served through the version picker maps to its line the same way: on a minor repository, a reader who chooses 0.21 is served the live 0.21 build. A list offers only the versions whose line is live, so a line not yet built, or retired, is left out of the menu, and a choice of it falls back to the reader's own version. The live mode offers every live line with no list at all. See .

section.title: A public site on the newest version, with older ones to choose
section.p: For product docs published per minor, where anonymous visitors should land on the newest version and may switch to older ones, set this once:
section.codeblock: curl -X PUT "$PUBLIC_URL/admin/api/repos/1/access" -H "$H" -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"access":"public","publicEntitlements":{"products":["core"],"features":[],"version":"latest"}}' curl -X PUT "$PUBLIC_URL/admin/api/repos/1/versions" -H "$H" -H 'content-type: application/json' \ -d '{"mode":"live"}'
section.p: With 0.21, 0.22 and 0.23 live, anonymous visitors get 0.23 at every address, with a menu of 0.23, 0.22 and 0.21. When the 0.24 build goes live it becomes the default and joins the menu, and a retired line leaves it, with no admin call. Signed-in readers start on their own organization's line and can switch the same way. To pin the versions instead, give a version such as "0.23" and {"mode":"list","versions":["0.23","0.22","0.21"]}, and update both after each release.
